key_insight: Reframed: on-die BIST cycling is the only cheap way to reach the 7e13-cycle hot-row endurance target in days. That measurement decides ~15 of 31 speculative triage verdicts.
killer_doubt: 200 variants share a ~10 mm2 slot, ~10k cells each, so tails resolve only to ~1e-4, not ppm. Logic MPWs cannot host the oxide or ferroic cells that matter.
decisive_experiment: One ~$150k shuttle: 10-20 variants x 1e5 cells, plus ZrO2/HZO MIM coupons post-deposited on top metal at <=400 C. Run on-die cycling to 1e13 and 85 C retention maps against an external pulse tester.
prior_art: Foundry/imec test vehicles and TEGs; RRAM-on-foundry-CMOS array chips (e.g., NeuRRAM 2022); Si gain-cell retention studies (Bar-Ilan, EPFL) [training knowledge].

key_insight: Composition-spread MIM libraries make dielectric screening fast and cheap. They are useful lab infrastructure, not an invention.
killer_doubt: Planar sputtered spreads do not predict ALD films in 60:1 holes. Known k 80-150 oxides (rutile TiO2, STO) leak ~1e-6 to 1e-5 A/cm2, and k 40->70 buys only 1.75x charge.
decisive_experiment: None worth funding standalone. If pursued, run ALD gradient libraries on Ru/RuO2 bottom electrodes for the 5 best DFT candidates (~$150k), judged at EOT <=0.4 nm and 1e-7 A/cm2.
prior_art: van Dover et al., Bell Labs, Nature 1998 (Zr-Sn-Ti-O spread); Intermolecular HPC programs with DRAM makers (Elpida); SNU Hwang group TiO2/STO [training knowledge].

key_insight: DFT can prune the oxide space before any deposition. But the k-bandgap trade-off is the real constraint, and the screen has already been run.
killer_doubt: No known oxide reaches k>=70 with Eg>=4 eV. DFT k for soft-mode oxides errs by ~30-50%, and thin-film dead layers cut k further. N-04 circuits give 10x versus 1.75x.
decisive_experiment: Re-mine the existing Materials Project dielectric set (~$20k): count ALD-growable phases above the k*Eg^2 frontier. Kill if fewer than 3 exist.
prior_art: Yim et al., NPG Asia Materials 2015 (automated ab-initio high-k screen, SNU); Petousis et al., Scientific Data 2017 (Materials Project dielectrics) [training knowledge].

key_insight: At 150 K, cooling costs ~3-7 W at the wall per W removed (versus ~10-19 at 77 K). SRH generation falls ~1e10, which could rescue leaky NAND-style poly-Si devices.
killer_doubt: Room-temperature IGZO already reaches aA leakage (>200 s at 95 C) with no cryostat. Field-driven GIDL and grain-boundary tunneling do not freeze out, and the 3D capacitor is still unsolved.
decisive_experiment: Cryo-probe poly-Si TFTs (university or NAND-like test structures, ~$100k) at 150 K and 2-3 V bias. Kill if off-current is >=1e-17 A or no better than IGZO at 300 K.
prior_art: Cryogenic DRAM (Rambus/Microsoft 2017, CryoRAM, CryoGuard); Kioxia cryogenic 3D NAND (Sanuki et al.); no cryogenic poly-Si 3D 1T1C found (via search snippet).

key_insight: Logic dies carry large, mostly idle capacitance. Making it addressable reuses area already paid for, a new framing of eDRAM.
killer_doubt: Decap is needed most during compute bursts, when scratch is busy. At on-die MIM density (~20-50 fF/um2), a 50 fF bit takes ~1 um2, ~50x an N3 SRAM cell.
decisive_experiment: PDN simulation (~$50k) of an accelerator under real di/dt traces, with 30% of decap switched out and switch ESR added. Kill if droop exceeds budget at any useful scratch size.
prior_art: IBM deep-trench eDRAM (POWER7-POWER9); Intel Crystalwell 128 MB MIM-cap eDRAM (22 nm); no dual-use decap memory found [training knowledge].

key_insight: A field-switched ion-in-cage dipole could make a bond-free, wear-free bit at ~1 nm2 with attojoule writes.
killer_doubt: Lowering a 0.8 eV barrier with dp~e*0.3 nm needs ~3 V/nm, 3x dielectric breakdown, before cage screening. Retention: ~27 s at 300 K, ~0.2 s at 85 C.
decisive_experiment: Low-temperature STM switching of single Li+@C60/C70 molecules on a gated substrate (~$200k, a university STM). Measure the switching field and barrier; kill if field exceeds 1 V/nm.
prior_art: Li+@C60 synthesized (Aoyagi et al., Nature Chem 2010); molecular charge memory (ZettaCore porphyrins, 2000s); N@C60 spin-qubit work [training knowledge].

key_insight: In a drawn and sliced bundle, capacitor height is set by slice thickness, not by etch aspect ratio.
killer_doubt: Drawable glasses have k~3-10 (ZrO2 ~40): a 30 nm coax gives ~1 fF/um, needing ~5 um slices. Metal cores break up far above 30 nm; bond pitch ~0.4-1 um.
decisive_experiment: Iterative stack-and-draw of a Sn/In-core borosilicate coax preform (~$150k, a fiber-draw lab). Report the smallest continuous metal core and the slice-face flatness. Kill above 200 nm.
prior_art: MIT Fink group multimaterial thermally drawn fibers; Yaman et al., Nature Materials 2011 (iterative size reduction, nanowire arrays) [training knowledge].

key_insight: KV data has a bounded useful life, so un-refreshed gain cells with in-array attention remove both refresh and HBM KV traffic. Decay-as-recency is a small twist on this.
killer_doubt: Decaying K/V magnitude is not ALiBi's additive logit bias. Leakage spans >10x across cells and drifts ~7%/C (Ea~0.6 eV), so decay is noise unless trained around.
decisive_experiment: Fine-tune a 125M-1B model (~$50k compute) with per-cell decay drawn from measured gain-cell leakage distributions plus temperature drift. Compare quality with a 2-bit KIVI digital KV baseline at matched bits.
prior_art: Leroux et al., Nature Comp. Sci. 2025: gain-cell KV store with analog attention and sliding window (via search snippet); RANA (ISCA 2018) data-lifetime eDRAM refresh.

key_insight: Capacitive via-stub coupling makes a transistor-less ROM in stacked BEOL planes with no DC sneak path. It is a neat cell for immutable weights.
killer_doubt: '4F2 at 40 nm' assumes an 80 nm metal pitch. Real 40 nm-node M1 pitch is ~120-140 nm, upper metals 2-4x wider: density ~5x worse than DRAM's 864 nm2.
decisive_experiment: Layout-accurate density plus SPICE coupling-margin study on a real 40 nm PDK (~$30k). If the margin is >=20 mV at 128 crossings, tape one MPW block.
prior_art: Apollo core rope; ROM compute-in-memory (YOLoC 2022, Hidden-ROM 2023); Taalas hardwired-weight silicon (per R16 source log) [training knowledge].

key_insight: Frozen weights need zero endurance and fill ~50-60% of HBM in MoE serving (est.). Mature-node ROM with one via mask per model could free that. Merge into the I-02186 dossier.
killer_doubt: SanDisk/SK hynix High Bandwidth Flash targets the same read-mostly weights with rewritable NAND ~10-30x denser than ROM. Model churn of 3-6 months strands mask sets.
decisive_experiment: Fleet economics model (~$100k): weight share of HBM by serving configuration, mask cost per model lifetime, and ROM versus HBF $/GB. Plus a 28/40 nm MPW testing 2-bit multi-level via resistance.
prior_art: Taalas HC1 hardwired Llama 8B (2026; AMD acquisition reported, per R16 log); SanDisk/SK hynix HBF (2025) [training knowledge].

key_insight: A filling-controlled Mott channel could give large current gain from a tiny stored charge, removing the high-aspect-ratio capacitor.
killer_doubt: 0.1 e/u.c. is ~7e13 cm-2 (~6 MV/cm in HfO2); a ~0.006 fF gate holding 300 e needs ~8 V. NdNiO3 is metallic at 300 K; IGZO gain cells suffice.
decisive_experiment: Solid-gated SmNiO3 or VO2 Hall bar, <=5 nm thick under a 3 nm HfO2 gate (~$150k, university oxide MBE/PLD). Kill if resistance swing is <10x at <=2 V.
prior_art: Mott-FET proposals (Newns et al., IBM 1998); SmNiO3/VO2 gating (Ramanathan); ferroelectric nickelate gating (Ahn, Yale; Triscone, Geneva) [training knowledge].

key_insight: Thick-oxide long-channel write devices in open PDKs give seconds of retention in a U.S.-fabbed node at near-zero capital. It is a good teaching and test vehicle.
killer_doubt: A 5 V 3T cell in 130 nm is ~5-10 um2, ~10,000x DRAM's 864 nm2. Retention drops ~10-30x at 85 C, so it does not move DRAM supply.
decisive_experiment: Not needed as an invention. Include it as reference cells on the I-01420 shuttle (~$10-20k) to calibrate the retention-tail BIST.
prior_art: Si gain-cell eDRAM (Teman/Giterman, Bar-Ilan; Meinerzhagen/Burg, EPFL); OpenRAM on SKY130 (Guthaus, UCSC) [training knowledge].
